cases.description: A one-shot civil time is resolved in its stored IANA zone and delivered once on time.
Changing the macOS system zone does not move a schedule that stored Asia/Shanghai.
The ambiguous New York 01:30 during fall-back resolves once using the earlier UTC instant.
The nonexistent New York 02:30 during spring-forward shifts by the exact one-hour gap to 03:30.
A late Monday workday alarm advances to Tuesday 09:00 civil time, not 24 hours after delivery.
An edit committed before the due transaction cancels the old occurrence and materializes revision 2.
A due transaction that commits first remains deliverable even when an edit follows in the same second.
Cancel committed before due disables the alarm and cancels regular and snooze occurrences.
Cancel after due commit stops recurrence but cannot recall the committed notification.
A ten-minute snooze is an absolute child occurrence and does not move the regular recurrence.
Replaying the same macOS notification action returns the existing snooze child.
A snooze and the next regular occurrence are distinct and both notify when due together.
Two due signals for the same canonical occurrence create one transaction, outbox row and logical notification.
Exactly 900 seconds late remains eligible and is dispatched within recovery tolerance.
At 901 seconds late the occurrence is terminally missed and never enters the notification outbox.
Long downtime marks old candidates missed, catches up only the current eligible one and preserves civil recurrence order.
A backward wall-clock correction before due re-arms the wait and cannot cause an early notification.
Moving wall time back across an accepted occurrence does not reopen it.
A forward correction crossing due by five minutes causes one immediate catch-up.
A restart before due reconstructs the timer from host persistence without changing identity.
A crash after outbox commit resumes the existing logical notification with the same identifier.
If the adapter may have accepted before a crash, retry uses put with the same ID and remains one logical notification.
A terminal accepted marker suppresses all adapter calls after restart.
Resume ten minutes after due creates one catch-up request within five seconds of recovery readiness.
Denied permission creates no outbox row, records a terminal denied outcome and does not prompt in background.
Granting permission later does not resurrect a denied occurrence but allows the next recurrence.
Transient failures retry at fixed offsets and accept on the third attempt with one logical ID.
Three failed adapter attempts terminate the occurrence while recurrence remains enabled.
The persisted host projection notifies even when all three guest event attempts trap.
Successful activation switches guest routing but does not replace a pending host occurrence.
A migration failure before activation leaves the old route, KV revision and pending alarm unchanged.
Post-activation rollback restores the old guest/KV route while preserving the terminal effect ledger.
During the rollback window schedule edits are frozen, while a host-owned notification snooze remains durable.

expected.rollback_result: edit-rejected; host-owned snooze survives any generation rollback

cases.description: A shadow/old generation cannot edit or cancel a live host schedule.
Launching an installed alarm app restores its host-rendered view and reads daemon state only.
A second launch intent focuses the existing alarm route instead of creating another view or scheduler.
Navigating away or closing the app view changes presentation only.
Explicit GUI quit leaves the daemon-owned schedule live and it notifies with no GUI process.
Opening the alarm app while the daemon is down shows unavailable state and creates no in-process timer owner.
Two isolated worlds submit the same canonical configure command through GUI and CLI and reach identical semantic daemon state.

expected.rollback_result: not-applicable; both worlds remain gen-1 and semantically equal

cases.description: A CLI disables and re-enables a recurring alarm without UI; the daemon cancels revision 1 and materializes revision 3 from civil time.

expected.rollback_result: not-applicable; no generation or app KV change

cases.description: Enabling an expired disabled one-shot through CLI is rejected without a revision, occurrence or UI side effect.

expected.rollback_result: not-applicable; generation and app KV unchanged

cases.description: CLI status returns normalized daemon state without launching a view, activating a generation or mutating alarm state.
Disabling an installed app is a daemon lifecycle transaction that disables its alarms; it is not equivalent to closing the view.

expected.rollback_result: not-applicable; re-enabling the app does not re-enable this alarm

cases.description: Uninstall may proceed only after the daemon has durably disabled future alarms while preserving terminal delivery audit facts.

expected.rollback_result: not-applicable; alarm deactivation commits before package removal
